results.title: Terms · OpenRadView
results.content:
## Intended use

OpenRadView is a viewer for personal education with medical images you own or have permission to use. It has not been clinically validated. Do not use it for diagnosis, screening, monitoring, treatment, emergencies or decisions about care. It does not replace a doctor, a radiologist or other qualified health professional.

Images, orientation, measurements and reconstructions can be incomplete or wrong. Ask a qualified clinician to interpret your scans. If you think you need urgent help, contact local emergency services.

## AI agents [...] ## AI agents

The app has no AI of its own and gives no opinion. You can connect an MCP-capable agent you already use, on your own account. Its replies are experimental AI commentary from that agent and its provider, can be wrong and do not replace professional interpretation. Provider terms apply to data you approve for sharing. An app permission dialog does not itself establish legal compliance or guarantee provider privacy.

## Example scans

The included examples are public research data under their own Creative Commons licenses, credited on the home page. Reuse follows those licenses and the TCIA data usage policy. Do not try to identify or contact the people in them.

## Liability [...] ## Liability

The app and this website are provided as is, and the warranty and liability terms of the GPL apply to the software. Liability exclusions apply only to the extent permitted by applicable law. Nothing here limits rights you have that cannot be waived under applicable law.

results.title: OpenRadView · Free DICOM viewer for CT, MRI and X-rays
results.content:
Built for Apple Silicon · runs on Windows too

# View your CT, MRI and X-rays

OpenRadView is a free, open-source viewer for opening and exploring your own medical images on your computer.

A personal research project for education, not clinically validated. Ask a clinician to interpret your scans; do not use the app for care decisions.

Crosshair: choose the same point in all views. Images [S] or ↑↓: move a plane.

The viewer

## Explore images on your computer

Three public example scans come with the app, so you can explore views before opening your own.

### Your files, opened locally

DICOM, NIfTI-1/2 and ZIPs, including multi-gigabyte studies. Imports stay local; archives are read without extraction.

### Window and level [...] ### Your agent asks

A local MCP-capable client you already use requests access. Nothing is shared yet.

### Review and allow

The app shows the recipient, series, preview, tools and risks. Allow covers one series or reviewed views.

### Revoke any time

Revoke, change series or quit to end access. Copies already sent cannot be recalled.

Replies come from your agent, not from OpenRadView. Treat them as experimental AI commentary: they can be wrong and do not replace a clinician.

Your agent may send what you share to its provider. Logs, retention and training depend on that provider's terms and settings; the app cannot enforce them. Removing metadata does not remove identifying details inside the pixels. Revoking access stops future requests but cannot recall copies already shared. [...] ### Measurements

Measure distance and angle where physical geometry is known. Rectangle statistics report scalar values or separate RGB channel codes.

Intended use

## For learning, not for diagnosis

It displays your images without interpreting them. Ask your doctor what they show.

### Good for

### Not for

Optional

## Bring your own AI agent

OpenRadView has no AI of its own and gives no opinion. It only offers an MCP connection, so an agent you already use, on your own subscription or a local model, can see a view you allow. MCP support is required.

On your subscription

Local models

Any client that supports local MCP servers works. Ollama runs the model, so pair it with an MCP-capable client or agent harness. Names and logos belong to their owners.

OpenRadView opens the DICOM and NIfTI files from your scan CD or zip on your own computer: linked axial, coronal and sagittal views, experimental 3D and measurements. Optional MCP access for your own AI agent. It is a personal research project for education and has not been clinically validated. Ask a qualified clinician to interpret your scans; do not use the app for decisions about care.

 Overview
 Reviews
 Alternatives
 Team
 More

Free

Launch tags:Education•Artificial Intelligence•GitHub [...] Point it at the disc, the zip or a folder, and it opens the DICOM or NIfTI files on your computer. You get linked axial, coronal and sagittal views, oblique planes, experimental 3D, and distance and angle measurements. No account, no telemetry, no upload.   
  
It's free, open source, and written in Rust with egui and wgpu, so images render on the GPU: Metal acceleration on Apple Silicon, and it works on Windows and Linux with a dedicated GPU too.

There's no AI inside. If you want, an agent you already use, or a local model, can connect over MCP and ask to see a view. Nothing is shared until you allow it, and the agent's replies can be wrong. [...] It's a personal research project, not certified medical software. If something feels wrong, see a doctor and keep asking questions. Ask a clinician to interpret your scans.  
  
It's an app I hope you never need.
